answer: An onyx island guards an agent economy with Catalan lantern-hoisting: each new identity must hoist lanterns up a cliff to the zenith, on the Catalan count, so the first fake hoists 1 lantern, the second 2, the third 5, the tenth 16,796 and the twentieth 6,564,120,420, and twenty fakes hoist 8,987,428,466 in all. Bulk farming fails because one keeper hoists one lantern at a time and each flame is lit only from the lantern before it, so no lantern can be hoisted in parallel or bought; like a chain where each flame lights only the next, the cost of the next fake always outruns the last.
